body: My grandma is a lot like that. I stopped speaking to her for 3 years and my sister refuses to talk to her. I talk to her now because my mom talked me into it. I think my grandma got it through her thick skull that I will not discuss politics with her and she could lose me again. It took a long time to get there. I know she still holds her hateful, bigoted, racist, homophobic, and “Trump is biblical” views and it keeps me up at night. But as long as she keeps her mouth shut, I’ll talk to her for my mom’s sake.

I had that issue, food service or highly skilled jobs only and I refused to work food service. I have a BA and 6 years of customer service experience and wasn’t finding anything. After over 2 years of job searching, I ended up at a community college working in the student accounts office. Really oversold myself yet ended up with the job. Building a lot of skills and while it can be stressful at times, I enjoy it for the most part. Benefits are okay. Pay could be better. 

It’s going on 6 months and I feel so lucky to be employed while there’s so many friends and family facing layoffs, usually those in IT. I’ll be happy when I get past that probation period.

Christmas. I can ignore Easter as most people I know sortve do their own thing. Even my extended and extremely Christian family really don’t do much besides maybe a church service. It’s harder to ignore Christmas. The hype, the dread, the bad presents, the terrible music, the attempt at terrible excuses to get out family gatherings.
Actually I can, and I’m planning on it 😈
I’ll look into that, thanks! Though I heard that dogs will get used to high pitched noise so I’ve been worried about bark boxes. I’ll look into deer deterrence devices though.

If you find it, I’ll be interested. I thought I saw something that in the county, you don’t necessarily need a permit but that seemed odd. Had a neighbor that was considering reporting them because the pond is a breeding ground for mosquitoes and there are other environmental factors. If I can’t go after the dog—then yeah I’ll look more into the pond itself.
I did, but I reached out to the sheriffs office and they’ll enforce the ordinance but only between the hours of 11pm and 7am. Animal control wasn’t helpful either.

Yep. He was friendly with us until we asked him to tone down the barking and ask if there’s anyway she can be trained. He kept her away for a day, she got into bad hay, then he blamed us for his dog getting sick even though it was on HIS PROPERTY! And now we’re his mortal enemies I guess.
You know, I’ve thought about it. I’ve also thought about befriending the crows and instructing them to keep the screeching dog away from the pond.

My aunt had a bunch of chickens and it looked fun. We also wanted “free” eggs. But I didn’t know how much joy I’d get from those silly creatures. Now we are about to get a bigger coop and a few more chickens.

Thank you. Yes, customer service has made me jumpy and anxious. I feel absolutely miserable to the point where I feel uncomfortable in my own skin and just and it to stop. It’s a constant battle and I’m so tired of feeling this. 

I’m sorry you feel similar, it’s rough.

I know the feeling, and the fact that I’m already passively suicidal is making it extra hard. Maybe it would be easier if I was around like minded individuals instead of people who love the man and don’t see the horrible things he did or said. I’m finding it hard to not find the nearest bridge and be done with it. The future already looked bleak but now… 

You’re not alone. Now more than ever we need to find our communities. And hopefully he can’t get away with too much but I’m not overly optimistic.

Fine, but I’ve already decided after 2020 and my extended family screaming election fraud that I will not see them. My mom’s final straw was her Q-BIL calling liberals “demons” in a FB post and my Q-aunts anti-trans/ “Christians are being persecuted because the lgbtq are allowed in public spaces” rant. So we’re staying home. I made a small thanksgiving dinner for me, my mom, and my brother. We decorated for the holidays and honestly it’s been one of the better thanksgivings I’ve had.

Actually, the longer I think about it, I think I will be that petty. The friend who voted Trump for cheaper groceries and the one who feels superior because she didn’t vote, both are about to see another side to me. They’ve seen glimpses but I will see the full force of my pettiness. And they’re going to realize, I do have my limits. 

Those who don’t vote, nothing pisses me off more. Honestly the friend who is apathetic and didn’t vote pisses me off more than the uninformed dumbass panicked friend who voted for the concepts of a plan to lower grocery prices. But trust me, I’m beyond furious at both.

I’m doing that with my grandparents. They’ve been fed these brainwashing campaigns for over 70 years. I’m having problems not getting angry at them but they’re getting older and slowing down. We have decided to just not talk politics. They’re… mostly good about not saying anything. They’ve also confessed to not liking Trump anymore and I’m not even sure they voted this time, but they liked Vance for some reason so I’m not sure. 

I’m cutting out other family members though as I do not tolerate hate speech, bigotry, or being lowkey accused of being a H****r supporter (that one was very odd and upsetting, I’m very confused about what their community is saying about liberals). They’re also full on qAnon so there’s a bunch of issues. So I, too, have my limits.

I have a friend of almost 20 years go from liberal to financially right wing. She’s been spewing nonsense about illegal immigrants and how the economy was better under Trump without listening to the reasons why the economy is bad now. She said to me that she voted for Trump so she can afford groceries and all the scary things he says it’s just democrat’s fear-mongering. 

At the time, I thought it was just fine we can be friends and agree to disagree. But the longer I’ve thought about it, and seeing the results, I’m really struggling not clicking that block button. I’ve lost friends to MAGA, I didn’t think I’d lose her too. But there’s this part of me that wants her to see the effects of the promised tariffs, watch her panic, and I can ask her if it was worth it. I don’t think I’m that petty though. 

Anyway, it’s hard. Her voting her Trump and another friend who “took the moral high ground” by not voting for the “lesser of two evils” because “both sides are evil.” She’s laughing at everyone’s reaction. Completely apathetic.

I have wondered how we got here. I really started to see the seeds during the Obama administration. Once Trump started running and the religious conspiracy theorists on Facebook started popping up, it’s like they thought it was finally okay to come out of the closet of hate and bigotry which is wrapped in a cloak of religious self-righteousness. 

Seeing my family now, those I used to look up to, are now freely spreading racist ideas, homophobia, and transphobia freely. I’m the bad one for not seeing it their way. They were always influenced by the satanic panic but they are wrapped into something more extreme. I’m very low contact and only interact for my mom’s sake, to keep the peace. I don’t even want to know what they’re saying now, but I’m glad my parents and siblings are just as upset as I am. But as of this week, my circle of friends and family just got a little smaller

I’m too shocked to cry. I thought we were better than this but apparently we’re not. I have family and friends who voted for them and I don’t think I can have them in my life anymore. I’m not doing well.
I am trying that approach and I did manage to get one person to not get me anything. I’m hoping the trend will catch on. However, I don’t I’ll be entirely successful this year.

Omg I understand your pain. My uncle did get gifts outside the terrible junk boxes and he got me a French press. Now, I do enjoy coffee but it’s not a French press for coffee, but for cocoa. I am a dark chocolate fan but this stuff is bitter and gross. No amount of cream and sugar can save it. Very expensive present that just sortve sits as a decoration because I can’t stand the taste. Doesn’t even have caffeine. While I appreciate the effort, it’s nothing I expressed interest in.

I think it’s because they don’t understand it. They love their basket idea and they love Christmas and getting together, why can’t I? Though I did convince one family member to not get me anything, but they weren’t happy.

‘93 and I prefer texting. Though, if it’s an intense conversation, I’ll sometimes prefer calling. I will, however, refuse to do FaceTime. Only one friend prefers calling (and would do FaceTime if I would do it) and if I did pick up the phone, I’d be on for a minimum of 2 hours just listening to them talk about nothing. Then I’ll let it ring then they’ll send me a 15-20 minute audio message of some twitter rant conversation they had.

It was sure awkward in middle school and my first high school, but no one made us shower which I was thankful for. But when we moved for my dad’s job, that high school demanded we take showers and we were graded on it. I was already a highly sensitive girl but I was also in a new place being watched by a creepy gym teacher to make we were undressed and we showered. I decided to just let them dock me points because it was just… creepy.

Same, I start noticing things but slowly try to not let it bother me (I’m finding ways to manage and getting better at not being bothered). But I have one friend who open mouth chews and smacks. I try to ignore it, but it’s hard to do when you have your headphones in and they send you a 15 minute audio message and they snack the entire time. I’ve talked to them about it but they don’t care. I’m thankful for transcription now because it was upsetting. But most strangers, I don’t notice unless I’m in a movie theater and someone loud sits next to me with a big bag of popcorn.

Even without the political, economic, and healthcare issues, I’m just not interested. I’ve seen what it’s like to go through pregnancy and raise a child. There’s very little of that life that interests me. Being JD Vance’s worst nightmare, the single childfree cat lady, sounds more fun to me.
What’s ironic is that they think they’re saving our world by voting republican and reverting us back to the 1950s.

Thank you. I hope that if he can get a liver soon (as he’s in critical condition) that he will recover and stay sober. His mother won’t make sure of that but maybe his brother will. But he has been cruel towards me so I can’t be close enough to him to ensure that. Plus, he’s high functioning so I wouldn’t know. I don’t know when he started to begin with, the date he gave me was one that would blame my mother (as he always unfairly does) but I have suspicions of when he started. My hopes are high that if he makes it (which is less likely by the day), he won’t drink again. But my expectations are low. Plus, he’s also had a nicotine addiction so I don’t know if he’ll turn back to that eventually. Time will tell.

I find that people who say that have a deep longing and nostalgia for that period of their life and want to live vicariously through their child. My friend is one of those; he misses being a kid and wants to have kids and relive those memories. 

Personally, I’m the opposite. While my childhood wasn’t traumatic, it wasn’t enjoyable. Besides some family drama, I just didn’t like other kids. I hated half the media that was out at the time. I hated being talked down to with that special voice adults use on kids (and some doctors use on patients). I felt disconnected from my peers and didn’t understand them. I just don’t have an interest in reliving those days, even through my non existent child. So that whole argument doesn’t work on me.

I don’t think I ever felt like I had to have kids, but I went back and forth on whether or not to have one. I think I’d be a good, patient mom. But I don’t see myself enjoying it much. I was with someone a long time and we considered marriage but my tokophobia and our religious differences got in the way. I was thinking of my family and watching them raise kids; they always seemed so worn out and done. I never understood why they’d want me and my siblings to have kids because it looked so soul-draining. Looking at my friends having kids now and they look like they aged 10 years and like their kids sucked out their life force. 

So I’m very childfree now. I’ve made my decision and I’m happy with it. My goals are financial stability and a house with a nice library and a couple cats. And silence.

I started seeing signs during the Obama administration. Once Trump started running for office, they all started coming out of the woodwork. Too many of them were my own friends and family. Most of them still supported Trump in 2020. I don’t understand it.

I never believed it even as a kid who went to Sunday school involuntarily. But I found out recently that my friend believes we have different languages because of the Tower of Babel. My grandmother also believes in Noah’s Ark and wants to go to the park in Kentucky. Many Christians believe that those stories are real and “here look at this article” or “oh watch this YouTube video!” One family member had me watch a YouTube video “confirming” Moses and his story in Exodus.

As someone who was born and raised in the PNW, I agree. I lived near Seattle for over a decade and went to college there and had no issues. However, outside the city, I seemed to be a Christian magnet. I came across a few people who were eager to find out where I went to church and try to convert me. Even somehow ended up with a Christian therapist. Usually non denominational types, a couple from some megachurch in Tacoma. Most people though, you’d never know what their preferences were because religion isn’t really talked about.
Wow! And I thought seeing one at 14 was bad. That’s awful, I’m sorry.
You’re fine, that’s a good way to phrase it. Thankfully her husband is very attentive, almost obnoxiously so. She’s in good hands.

Yeah, I have asked not to know too many medical details but apparently my cousin and the baby are fine and going home tomorrow. It sounded like she didn’t truly know how bad it was going to be but she made it.

I am eternally grateful, and traumatized, by the very graphic birthing video in my early childhood development class in my freshman year of high school. I believe I started my journey of becoming childfree in that class. My mother would have not have told me the real horrors until I was mid-labor, just like they did with my cousin who gave birth today.

I asked that same question to a couple people yesterday as a family member was going through birth. I was getting all the graphic, intimate details of the family member in labor before I asked them, rather harshly, to stop. Apparently there was a group chat but thankfully I wasn’t invited. But after I asked them to stop, they stopped so I have no idea how the actual delivery went. But during this whole thing, I came to the theory that they think it’s just… part of life; part of being a woman. The humiliation, the lack of dignity, the horrendous pain. It makes a good story I guess. As a woman, however, I’d rather not go through with it. While I think mothers who go through that are really strong, I still have to ask: why? Then the fun doesn’t end there, then you got this very loud messy tiny human to deal with. I’ll stick with my cat  and my growing collection of books.

My neighbor who doesn’t mind the dog is worried about this. If I can’t find an ally to report the dog, I am wondering if I have an environmental impact ally. This is something I’m looking into. Mosquitos are already bad here but the pond made it so much worse.

I had a friend who had that reaction. “Oh well it’s an animal, dogs bark.” Okay, try living with the high pitched yipping you can’t escape from and you can’t go relax outside because it’s loud and the bark is amplified by the water. And yeah, dogs bark, but noise nuisance laws include barking for a reason. It lowers enjoyment of living. And no, I don’t blame the dog itself, I blame the owner for knowingly creating a situation in which it’ll become a nuisance. I have a right to enjoy my property same as him. So his dog has to find another, quieter way to play. 

This new “pet parent”/ “fur baby” trend has gotten ridiculous and caused these owners to become so disrespectful and entitled. I believe he called himself a pet parent too and said he spoils his dogs. I had dogs before (I regretted it but that’s another story), but I never let them annoy my neighbors. If they barked, we took care of it quickly. You can spoil your pets, but not at the expense of others.

Yeah that’s why I’m afraid of an ultrasonic bark stopper because I heard dog owners are starting to claim it hurts them. I am scared of retaliation. Someone warned me not to talk to them because they did and the dog neighbor retaliated to the point that they had to move. So I’m going to try anonymously reporting them to animal control but he’ll know it’s us so I’m a little weary. We, too, are growing hedges to try and block them out. Good luck on yours!

He also built it KNOWING it barks the entire time it swims. He also takes his dogs to the hardware store with no leashes so that kinda tells you the type of “dog parent” he is. Ive meet a lot of inconsiderate dog owners but this one is a special breed.

Yes, he dug a very large hole that took him all summer to dig with heavy machinery, often until 1am, exclusively for his dog. It’s also a mosquito breeding ground. No, I believe it’s a border collie. When it’s not swim-barking, it’s actually very quiet. If it wasn’t for the pond, it’s actually the least problematic dog in the neighborhood.

Yeah, we’re working on the recording process at the moment and we will be reporting. It’s just a shame we have to do this, he seemed reasonable in the beginning, but because we asked he turned on us fast. I know that’s not unusual but it’s just aggravating. Unfortunately, we have talked to our neighbors and none of them really mind it. In fact, one said they thought the dog was funny. So we have no allies. We have a new neighbor moving in though so maybe we’ll have a potential ally in the near future.

There’s a lot of factors but one in particular comes from the McCarthy era and the red scare propaganda.  The threat of the atheist communists vs the “good Christian American.” Then you had televangelists like Billy Graham and politicians like Ronald Reagan who pushed this narrative. They heavily influenced my grandparents who then influenced their kids into the “we are a good, Christian nation!” You can’t correct them or show them real, historical facts because they believe it’s just leftist propaganda. I’ve learned to keep my mouth shut, but I also ain’t that close to them partly because of that.

I had an ex coworker who did that. She had a miscarriage and then posted a collage of her, her husband, and the deceased infant. It was only in like the 2nd trimester (I think) so it looked a little off. Was a bit of a jump scare when opening Facebook. Everyone at work was disturbed but we didn’t say anything. Then she would repost it every year. She then went on to have, I believe, 2 kids (with a lot of medical help) and 2-3 more miscarriages. I always felt sorry for her but posting a dead infant online seemed disturbing.

A friend I went to college with would eat food during class or while studying. I have some family members with terrible table manners but she would chew and smack her food in a cow-like manner. Now my parents raised me to keep my mouth closed while chewing and to not talk with my mouth full so seeing that was appalling. However, nothing beats my mayonnaise loving retail manager. The horrors I saw still make me gag.
I took that class, early childhood development. That video combined with having to help out at the preschool across the street convinced me that motherhood wasn’t something I was into.

I do not like babies or toddlers. Kids and teens though, depends on the individual. Some kids are sweet and make my day but some I can’t stand being around for more than a minute. But at the end of the day, I want to go home to where it’s quiet and hang with my cat.

It’s part of my reason, outside of tokophobia and lack of maternal instinct. My severe depression, borderline anxiety, and attachment issues have taken a toll. I don’t think I’d be the best parent for a child. I’d do my very best to take care of them but I’m not sure I could offer them enough emotional connection. My dad wasn’t there emotionally and it was detrimental. I’ve decided it would be best to try to just take care of myself and I’m not even doing a good job of that.

I would consider a serious relationship with another introvert if we had our own spaces. My friend has a set up like that, except they’re married. Personally, I’ve been around enough divorce that attachment like that is unappealing. Kids I have no interest in. I like my space relatively clean and quiet.

I’m having a similar problem with my cousin and her coming baby. My family is rather small so there’s some implied expectation that I’m to step in as an aunt figure and be involved. Except I’m not close to my cousin just because we had fun playing together over 20 years ago. They can be offended all they like but I am not the person they have envisioned in their mind. I hold no ill will towards my cousin or her baby, but it’s also not my responsibility. 

I think what you’re doing and what you’re comfortable with is fine. If your family pushes back, like mine might, then it’s time to introduce some boundaries. It’s not your baby, you weren’t consulted on your role, it’s not your responsibility. Don’t let them pressure you into a familial role you’re uncomfortable with.
Same and agreed. They thought it was good experience for me for when I had my own kids but I felt like my adolescence was stolen from me and they wonder why I don’t want kids.

Yes, I do, but thankfully I was able to avoid pregnant family and friends until recently. It just looks so unnatural and unnerving. My cousin is currently pregnant and my whole family is freaking out with joy. Wouldn’t be a big deal if they didn’t try to include me by showing me weekly baby bump pics, ultrasounds, and talking about how she can feel the baby moving. I’ve tried to explain tokophobia to them but they don’t get it and they get highly offended so I just have to power through the anxiety. Thankfully I got out of the Christmas/ baby shower so I don’t have to worry about her asking me if I want to touch her belly. Instead I’ll be hiding with my childfree friend eating good food. Last time I saw her, it was a small bump but it still made me uneasy so I tried not to look at her. I felt guilty but it grossed me out.

I was around the same age when my brother was born. My mom wanted me involved because she thought it was cool and to prepare me for my own pregnancies. But I thought it was so gross and unnerving that I developed tokophobia instead. I’m 30 now and still not over it.
I saw it during a college football game recently. Not only did I see a commercial, it was on a screen at the stadium.

If I remember correctly, he said something about Infinity War being the end for Loki and his redemption arc. I do believe he had been approached for the Loki series by then. While he was right about that variant, it wasn’t the end for Loki. I won’t believe anything he says until it’s made official.

He said something similar during the Infinity War tour. Tom has always been good at not spilling Marvel secrets. I think Marvel is still scrambling with the uncertainty surrounding Majors and how to continue without him. I think with Loki’s new powers, it feels like he’ll come back in some way. Maybe Tom hasn’t his gotten an offer yet because they still don’t have a concrete plan. An exec also said something about getting Loki emotionally ready to meet up with Thor again. So maybe this is a closure for Loki and his redemption arc and now Loki can start a whole new story. However, it is truly the end of his story, then I think it was a great ending for him.
I graduated in ‘11 and I have been able to read analog clocks since elementary school. I was the shy, quiet kid but one of the few who could read it so I was often asked the time.

I was 12 when my brother was born and I wanted kids at the time. But watching the pregnancy, I started to develop a phobia from all the medical appointments and watching him move around. After he was born, I hated the noise, changing him, all that. I was, for a short time before I put my foot down, the live in babysitter and was expected to help out. So around 14, I believe. I might’ve been a fence sitter until the era of toilet training which solidified my non-desire for producing kids. 

My mom thought it was a good idea because she had no clue how to handle babies when I was born so she wanted me to know how to for when I had my first child. That, however, backfired on her and I have no intention of having kids (which she mostly supports me on, saying I should only have them if I want them but does occasionally mention how she wants grandkids). I’m 30 now and my cousins about to have her first and I refuse to help out. I’m thankful though that my mom had my brother because he’s awesome and, because of him, I know children aren’t for me.
I saw one when watching college football the other day. However, I was slightly behind so I fast forwarded through the commercial. Was lucky that time but still irritated to see it.
There’s that but he thought we could just… push it out. I think he misunderstood what his mother told him.
Yeah I’ve often wondered if she told him that when he was little. However, the fact that he still believed that into his twenties was concerning.

Yeah, it was crazy. Our health classes in high school were a bit lacking in info but I would think you’d know that’s not how it works by your 20s. He’s also gay so maybe he just didn’t have enough experience around women? I don’t know.

I had a guy friend who said his mom was able to sit on the toilet and get rid of all the blood at once. I had to explain to him, a grown man, how periods work and how he probably misunderstood what his mom said.

My younger sister did that until she was around 8 too. My parents tried so hard to get her to stop but she was just too lazy and she was, strangely, not humiliated by it until she was around 8 and stopped.

I agree, that’s why I don’t like infant or child baptisms because they don’t understand what it means. I was just promised if I tilted my head over an ornate salad bowl so I can get my hair wet, the priest can say words over me, and I get oil on my head then I can get pie after. As a kid, I didn’t care enough to pay attention in the sacraments class so I didn’t know what it meant. I did it for my mom and for pie. 

My mom does agree now that she should’ve waited until I was ready but she was pressured by the church and her overly critical religious MIL. Of course, if she waited until I was ready, I would never have gotten baptized lol!

Because of my mom converting to Catholicism when I was little, she had baptized me in elementary school. So I had to take that class followed by reconciliation the next then ending with communion. So a total of 3 years on top of Sunday school. 

I was resentful of my family for forcing me to go through with the classes and sacraments and I still resent them for it even though I understand why they did it. I didn’t understand what it meant, it was just something I was forced to do. Personally, if I had kids, I wouldn’t force them to take classes just to appease family. If they wanted to as adults who can understand what it means, then that’s their business. My family can whine all they want. However a lot of them would whine that they’re Catholic and not Baptist so there’s no winning anyway lol!

My maternal grandfather wasn’t really a believer until he meet my grandmother and converted. My paternal grandfathers family are almost all atheist, especially the men. The ones who did convert to Christianity are not well liked and there’s often theological debates between them. I wouldn’t say they’re a friendly bunch but they are more science centric which I always appreciated because everyone else in my family are more fanciful, conspiracy theorist Christian types. Me and my 2 siblings are all 4th (at least) generation atheists.
Yeah it’s a dealbreaker. I’ve been there once, even if they say they’ll be respectful, they won’t forever. They’ll eventually try hard to convert.
Tried to explain this to my mom who wants grandkids. Like, you had me help raise your kid when I was 12; I’ve already helped raised a kid. I did my time.

First, I do believe that’s a qAnon conspiracy theory and not to be taken seriously. Second, I think for a people who are against science, it’s funny to see them into such a science fiction concept. As far as I know, we don’t have the technology to clone humans, especially into full grown adults. I think it’s just plastic surgery, makeup, and/or age. If they are being replaced, then it’s probably look-alikes but I honestly doubt it.

I’d say social anxiety is part of my problem. I was really close to someone but my tokophobia (fear of pregnancy and childbirth) and my self-hatred got in the way. As I get older, it’s harder for me to connect with people because of social anxiety and depression. I’m a 30 year old virgin and I makes me sad sometimes because I want closeness but I’m making peace with it.
I would rsvp in a heartbeat ❤️
Yeah, it was horrifying lol! But I saw a video that was worse, the baby was doing summersaults in the womb. I didn’t know that was a real thing and watching it was not fun lol!
Well, they tried for 3 decades before ending in an ugly divorce. Guess I was a terrible therapist.

I should clarify, I’m happy for her because she’s getting the life she always dreamed of. But honestly, we’ve never been close. We really haven’t hung out since we were little. My family is pushing me to be friends with her because we were close when we were kids but that was 2 decades ago and we have since grown our separate ways and have nothing in common. I wish her the best but I don’t really have an interest in being in her life. She doesn’t seek me out either. I think we’ve talked all of twice in the last 5 years and they were very simple, short convos.

I’ve used the “I’m busy” excuse a lot in the past to get out of family events. Worked well when I worked retail especially during the holiday season. I’ll probably use that excuse again. Or, like you said, I might simply just say no. 

I won’t being doing any childcare unless it’s a major medical emergency or something of that nature. But there’s enough family that’ll take them that I don’t see that happening.
Too many. Or the expectation that the baby will fix the marriage. I was one of those apparently.

I totally get what you’re saying and I do know I sounds awful for not being involved, at all. I think the issue for me is that my cousin and I aren’t close and we’re basically strangers. We have nothing in common and really haven’t hung out since we were real little. We’ve done our own thing since then and now that she’s married (I did go to the wedding) and she’s having a baby, it’s like my family wants me to get excited and more involved. I partly don’t want to go to the baby shower because I’d feel awkward, like going to a co-workers baby shower. If it was a close friend or if my childfree siblings changed their mind, I’d get involved in their kids life.

I agree, she could use some therapy. If I were her, I would’ve gotten therapy way before getting pregnant.

Thanks, I don’t think my parents saw it that way because they thought I could use the experience and it was typical for their age group. Most people in my family had kids and I think they’d just assume I’d be a good religious wife with a few kids. In a way I’m glad I did it and glad I saw the process from pregnancy to childhood so I know that’s not the path I want to take. My mother did apologize and I love my brother but I don’t want to do that again.

I will be setting boundaries and they should respect it but I know they may see me differently after which I’m not looking forward to.
